PMID:32405202.setting: Leicester Orthopaedics, University Hospitals of Leicester
PMID:32405202.standard: Anatomical reduction assessed by Pettrone's radiological criteria

cycle1.result: Malreduced fixation in 25% of cases; inadequate restoration of fibular length was the most common malreduction.

PMID:32405202.intervention: Regional teaching and dissemination of infographic posters.
PMID:32405202.other_findings: No significant differences in age, gender or time to surgery between phases.

PMID:30199962.topic: Benzodiazepine and Z-drug prescribing in older inpatients
PMID:30199962.setting: Surgical and medical wards, Sligo General Hospital (general hospital)
PMID:30199962.standard: Evidence-based consensus guidelines on benzodiazepine and Z-drug prescribing in older adults

cycle1.result: Prevalence of benzodiazepine/Z-drug use 54% (38/70); 36% (25/70) started before admission.

PMID:30199962.intervention: Audit results and consensus guidelines sent to all GPs in County Sligo; educational sessions for doctors and nurses.

cycle2.dates: Six months after the original audit
cycle2.result: Prevalence 46% (32/70), not statistically significant; started before admission 23% (16/70).

PMID:30199962.other_findings: Discharge summaries were screened at six weeks to assess prescribing on discharge.

PMID:33931281.topic: Arthroplasty service configuration and same-day discharge
PMID:33931281.setting: Academic medical centre and associated community-based hospital (Brigham and Women's, Boston)

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:33931281.intervention: Primary uncomplicated TJA and UKA moved to the community hospital; complex cases kept at the academic centre; same-day discharge and rapid recovery protocols introduced.
PMID:33931281.other_findings: Community hospital volume rose 36.7% (+239) with improved quality metrics; net margins 3.6% and 18.8% higher for THA and TKA.

cycle1.result: Serious complication in 27.5% (n = 83); AUROC CFS 0.77, CCI 0.71, ACS NSQIP Calculator 0.76.

PMID:42584172.other_findings: CFS was fastest to administer (median 9.5 s vs 98.5 s for ACS NSQIP Calculator).

PMID:33278206.setting: Single institution (authors at University of California Davis Medical Center, Sacramento)
PMID:33278206.standard: American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Improvement Program best-practice guidelines: antibiotic order and administration within 1 hour

cycle1.result: Baseline period; figures not given in abstract.

PMID:33278206.intervention: First, institutional awareness and education of departments; second, tracking of antibiotic order and administration times with quarterly audits following new guidelines.

cycle2.result: Antibiotic order within 1 hour and administration within 1 hour both significantly improved after the second initiative, as did median arrival-to-order and arrival-to-administration times (figures not given in abstract).

PMID:33278206.other_findings: Three periods were compared; neither measure improved after the first, education-only initiative.

PMID:26388003.setting: Department of Hand Surgery, Singapore General Hospital

cycle1.result: 97% successfully resected arthroscopically; recurrence 10% (3 cases); grip strength 27 kg to 32 kg; VAS pain 0.8 to 0.3.

PMID:26388003.other_findings: No major complications; range of motion unchanged.

EPMC:PMC:PMC7989631.topic: Secondary prevention of fragility fractures after hip fracture
EPMC:PMC:PMC7989631.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic unit, University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire

cycle1.dates: Pre- and post-UK lockdown (dates not given)
cycle1.result: Pre-lockdown vs lockdown: orthogeriatric review 88% to 0%; vitamin D/calcium 81.6% to 58.0% (p = 0.0156); bone-sparing medication 60.7% to 18.2% (p = 0.0037); DEXA requests 40.1% to 3.6% (p = 0.0027).

EPMC:PMC:PMC7989631.intervention: Introduction of the 'MRS BAD BONES' mnemonic for secondary fracture prevention.

cycle2.result: Vitamin D/calcium 85.7% (p = 0.0034); bone-sparing medication 72.4% (p = 0.0002); DEXA requests 60%; orthogeriatric review 38%.

EPMC:PMC:PMC7989631.other_findings: Orthogeriatricians were redeployed during the COVID-19 lockdown.

PMID:23070220.setting: All 22 Scottish orthopaedic units (Musculoskeletal Audit, Scotland)
PMID:23070220.standard: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) principles for hip and knee arthroplasty

cycle1.result: 8 (36%) units had an ERAS programme; urinary catheterisation 468/1,345 (35%).

PMID:23070220.intervention: Input and support from a national steering group (nationally guided ERAS programme).

cycle2.result: 15 (68%) units had an ERAS programme; urinary catheterisation 337/1,278 (26%) (p = 0.03).

PMID:23070220.other_findings: ERAS patients mobilised same day more often (36% vs 4%), had shorter stay (median 4 vs 5 days) and ERAS knee patients had fewer transfusions (2% vs 13%).

PMID:33573901.setting: AUGMENT collaborator sites and British Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society congress 2018

cycle1.result: Consensus on Weber B management; CT used for posterior malleolus injuries by 97.50% of foot and ankle specialists vs 69.79% of others.

PMID:33573901.other_findings: Foot and ankle surgeons were more likely to operate on posterior malleolus fractures.

PMID:37141798.setting: All 17 Scottish units performing revision knee arthroplasty (SCOTnet)
PMID:37141798.standard: Current national guidelines for unit case volume per year and recommended individual surgeon case volumes

cycle1.result: 5/17 (29%) units met national case volume guidelines; 11/77 (14%) surgeons met recommended individual volumes; 37/77 (48%) surgeons did 2 or fewer cases per year.

PMID:37141798.other_findings: Revision for infection 147/506 (29%); RKCC R1 43%, R2 45%, R3 12%.

PMID:21561759.setting: Surgical foot and ankle department, Great Western Hospital, Swindon (district general hospital/treatment centre)

cycle1.result: 974 (86%) referred by GPs; 65% progressed to surgery; 66 (5.8%) needed no intervention.

PMID:21561759.other_findings: Authors suggest referral guidelines between GPs and the service.

PMID:15756078.setting: Department of Orthopaedics and Trauma, Wishaw General Hospital

cycle1.result: True scaphoid fracture 6.66% (5/75); 80% had no bony injury but were immobilised and followed up (128 casts, 135 X-ray sets, 135 clinic appointments).

PMID:15756078.other_findings: Ten patients (13.33%) had other wrist injuries.

PMID:33914632.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic Department, Wirral University Hospital Trust (elective patients)
PMID:33914632.standard: Montgomery v Lanarkshire Health Board (2015) standard for informed consent

cycle1.result: Specific patient risks documented 50%; procedure-specific risks 42%; alternative options 48%; written information 14%.

PMID:33914632.intervention: Results presented to clinicians and a teaching session on expected consent standards.

cycle2.result: Specific patient risks 60%; procedure-specific risks 76%; alternative options 66%; written information 8%.

PMID:33914632.other_findings: Copied letters to patients in only 12% across cycles; dedicated consenting clinics outperformed standard clinics.

PMID:12667850.setting: Department of Neurology, University of Tuebingen

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:12667850.other_findings: Not an audit; fMRI study of rate-dependent brain responses during auditorily cued finger tapping.

PMID:34821224.setting: Spanish National Hip Fracture Registry compared with national Minimum Basic Data Set

cycle1.result: No significant differences in patient variables; significant differences in care process variables (operated, deceased, procedures, postoperative stay) compared with 83,110 CMBD cases.

PMID:34821224.other_findings: Better care process results in the registry attributed to participation bias.

PMID:24457386.standard: Five proposed audit criteria: daily delirium risk assessment with a valid tool; daily environment assessment; essential nursing care; clinical criteria to confirm delirium; non-drug before drug interventions

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:24457386.other_findings: Paper develops evidence-based audit criteria; no audit data reported.

PMID:31567556.setting: Orthopaedic trauma department, tertiary teaching hospital (Nanfang Hospital), Guangzhou
PMID:31567556.standard: JBI best practice recommendations for pain relief during wound care

cycle1.result: Poor compliance with best practice (figures not given in abstract).

PMID:31567556.intervention: Recommended changes implemented using the Getting Research into Practice barriers and strategies (details not given).

cycle2.result: Significant improvements after implementation, but not adequately maintained at the second follow-up audit.

PMID:31567556.other_findings: Two follow-up audits over six months; patient pain scores improved (t = 2.272, P > 0.05).

PMID:17002853.topic: Secondary prevention of fragility fractures after hip fracture
PMID:17002853.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Royal Glamorgan Hospital
PMID:17002853.standard: British Orthopaedic Association guidelines for secondary prevention of fragility fractures

cycle1.result: FBC 26 (96%); LFT and bone profile 18 (66%); calcium and vitamin D 9 (30%); 1 patient referred for DEXA.

PMID:17002853.intervention: Awareness raised among junior doctors and nurse practitioners; AMTS above 7 used as DEXA criterion in over-80s; hospital protocol based on BOA guidelines.

cycle2.result: FBC and renal profile 100%; bone profile 28 (75.7%); LFT 34 (91.9%); treatment 24 (65%); DEXA referral 9/23 eligible (40%) (P = 0.03).

PMID:17002853.other_findings: 60% of patients still not referred for DEXA; a fracture liaison nurse pathway was recommended.

EPMC:PMC:PMC3032141.topic: Combined rheumatology and orthopaedic foot clinic outcomes
EPMC:PMC:PMC3032141.setting: Combined rheumatology and orthopaedic foot and ankle clinic, Leeds Teaching Hospitals

cycle1.result: 41 (82%) had RA; 22 (53.7%) had surgery; pain VAS in operated foot 58.3 to 26.2 (p = 0.002).

EPMC:PMC:PMC3032141.other_findings: No change in foot scores in the non-surgery group.

PMID:31549413.setting: Emergency department, theatre and ward, Liverpool Hospital, Sydney

cycle1.result: Delirium on day 3: 49 (33%); bundle compliance ED 49 (33%), anaesthesia 40 (27%), orthogeriatrics 140 (93%).

PMID:31549413.intervention: Perioperative care bundle: fascia iliaca blocks, rationalised analgesia, avoidance of deliriogenic drugs, regular staff education and continuous compliance audit.

cycle2.result: Delirium on day 3: 33 (22%) (p = 0.04); bundle compliance ED 85 (59%), anaesthesia 104 (69%), orthogeriatrics 143 (95%).

PMID:31549413.other_findings: Adjusted OR 2.2 (95%CI 1.1-4.4) for avoiding delirium; no difference in 30-day mortality, morbidity, institutionalisation or walking.

PMID:38740278.setting: One district general hospital, Virtual Fracture Clinic (Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth)
PMID:38740278.standard: Timescales compared with 2018 local study (scan within 48 hours and one week; treatment decision within one week)

cycle1.result: Presentation to USS request 2.9 days; request to scan 6.8 days; 81% scanned within one week and 18% within 48 hours; presentation to treatment decision 10.9 days; 34.5% with plan within one week.

PMID:38740278.intervention: Revised pathway allowing investigation and referral to be initiated by other healthcare professionals.

cycle2.result: USS request 1.1 days; request to scan 3.2 days; 95% scanned within one week and 31.3% within 48 hours; treatment decision 6.2 days; 74.2% with plan within one week (p < .01).

PMID:38740278.other_findings: 0.8 fewer appointments per patient, estimated saving $10,110 ($128 per patient); 87.8% had a tear on USS.

PMID:25619809.topic: Syndesmosis screw fixation in Weber C ankle fractures
PMID:25619809.setting: Capital & Coast District Health Board, Wellington

PMID:25619809.other_findings: Practice did not vary with surgeon experience.

PMID:35509302.standard: Local departmental standards (ultrasound within one week of request; treatment decision within two weeks) and SMART protocol timeframes (scan within 48 hours)

PMID:36465496.standard: Hospital protocol: surgery within 24 h of last DOAC dose (if creatinine clearance >50 ml/min) with 1 g tranexamic acid at induction

EPMC:PMC:PMC8793471.setting: 43 centres in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland

PMID:40480335.topic: Medicare audit documentation for joint arthroplasty

PMID:19647251.topic: Hip fracture national audit of care standards

PMID:19647251.standard: Published national guidelines for hip fracture care in older people

PMID:24220529.topic: Hip fracture Best Practice Tariff compliance

PMID:41885398.standard: JBI best practice recommendation: no routine hip movement precautions after THR

PMID:35212120.topic: Cervical spine CT imaging in children

PMID:41842928.topic: Fracture risk assessment in PrEP users

PMID:41842928.standard: UK guidelines: fracture risk assessment for PrEP users aged over 50 (FRAX or QFracture)
